Responses tools across routes

Caller and hosted tools on Responses routes: Claude tool identity, Chat Completions tool-call shapes, repeated declarations, the tool search bridge, and hosted web search.

About 13 min read · 7 sections

On this page
01 Claude tool declarations and call identity 02 Chat Completions tool-call shapes 03 Tool naming and replayed calls 04 Rejections and empty completions 05 Repeated tool declarations 06 Tool search on the Codex subscription route 07 Hosted web search

Part of Responses support. The client owns tool execution; these are the rules for how tool declarations and tool calls travel on each route. Request plumbing and failure classes are on Responses protocol, streaming, and failures, and per-provider adapter behavior is on Responses provider adapters and images.

Claude tool declarations and call identity

The Claude adapter accepts text and inline-image messages, function calls and outputs, custom tool calls and outputs, and function/custom tools grouped in namespaces. It also accepts the older nested function definition format for existing Chat Completions clients.

Claude tool definitions become native virtual MCP declarations. Native calls return with their original name, namespace, and call ID. Custom tool input returns as a string rather than JSON-encoded function arguments. The caller validates and executes the tool; the gateway does not execute it or enforce grammar constraints. The private gateway MCP server loads before Claude begins inference. It disables nonblocking startup and marks its catalog alwaysLoad, keeping the caller action surface available at startup. Rejected Claude calls log fixed categories for unknown tools, internal search/wait helpers, duplicate IDs, malformed input, or a missing required call. Names and arguments are never included in those logs. Claude's private MCP names derive from the caller identity rather than its index in a particular request. Reordering, deferred tools, and forced-tool filtering therefore retain each binding. Replayed call/result names use those same native names without altering arguments, IDs, results, or message content. Native tool events can also use an exact caller alias or an unambiguous caller-local name; ambiguous names, stale numeric aliases, and foreign tools are rejected.

Exact aliases apply to translated call parsing and historical replay. A live Claude CLI must actually address its registered virtual MCP tool. Its early confinement guard therefore still rejects non-gateway native names, even when they resemble a caller alias. scripts/probe-claude-tool-identities.mjs verified with CLI 2.1.299 and a synthetic API that only the registered mcp__gateway__… name delivered the virtual relay result; bare native names and qualified/local caller aliases produced internal CLI tool errors instead. The probe executes no caller tool and uses no account or paid inference. Run it with --claude /absolute/claude --root /tmp/fresh-tool-identity-probe.

Chat Completions tool-call shapes

Chat Completions providers accept finish_reason: "stop" with tool calls only when the caller explicitly selects a named tool, matching vLLM's named-tool completion format. Every call still requires the selected tool identity, a unique nonempty ID, and valid object JSON; custom tools also require string input. Automatic, required, and disabled tool selection cannot complete with stop plus tool calls. Truncated streams and tool calls capped by length still fail. This applies to both Responses and Messages ingress.

A garbled call from a sampled Chat Completions model is a retryable failure, not a final one. An unknown tool name, invalid JSON arguments or invalid tool input fails the stream with malformed_tool_call, so Codex retries the request under its own stream retry limit and the model samples again. Gateway itself does not replay the request, and a caller that pins a temperature of zero can receive the same bad call again. Over Messages ingress the same failure arrives as api_error, and retrying is that client's decision. It checks every call in a batch before releasing any of them, because a client runs a call as it arrives and a retry would otherwise repeat a valid sibling. Identity faults that do not depend on sampling, such as a duplicate or missing call ID, a changed ID or an unselected tool, stay final as invalid_tool_call.

Local Qwen workers made this necessary. They returned names such as tool=, tool=tool_14 and tool_1=apply_patch, and the old final failure ended a worker's turn on one bad completion, which sent the parent to a paid fallback model.

Tool naming and replayed calls

Chat Completions providers receive each tool under its real name. A name the Chat Completions grammar forbids, a duplicate, or a name shaped like tool_N falls back to that tool's position. Opaque positions were the cause of Qwen's garbled calls: the model must write the name back token by token, and at the index token it was unsure what came next. Replaying 12 real failure contexts showed about a 6% chance of an invalid token per call with positions and about 0.004% with real names; lowering the temperature did not help. Gateway never maps a position back to a tool that has a real wire name, because that would be a guess. See the evidence.

The Anthropic API provider still addresses tools by position. On both, a replayed call can only stay structured when its tool is declared in the same request. Codex's local compaction replays the whole chat without its tools, and an MCP tool can be deferred or disconnected later in a chat. A replayed call to an undeclared tool therefore stays in the history as text, [Earlier tool call NAME: ARGUMENTS], and its result becomes [Result of earlier tool call NAME] followed by the output. Calls to declared tools keep their structured form. Before this change the whole request failed with "Historical tool is absent from the current catalog", so long Qwen chats could not compact. A current tool_choice that names an undeclared tool is still refused.

The same compaction request carries tool_choice but no tools. vLLM refuses that combination with HTTP 400 ("When using tool_choice, tools must be set"). For Chat Completions providers with no declared tools, auto and none both mean that nothing can be called, so the gateway omits the field. required and a named tool still fail, because no tool can satisfy them.

Rejections and empty completions

Every HTTP 400 from a Chat Completions server records chat_request_rejected with the provider id, a fixed reason (tool_choice_without_tools, context_length, output_tokens, reasoning_effort, tool_schema, model, message_format or unknown) and, when the server names one from a fixed list, the param. The server's message text is never recorded. scripts/e2e-chat-compaction.mjs checks the compaction shapes against a real provider before a release.

For Responses ingress, a Chat Completions reply that ends with stop but contains no answer text or tool call fails as incomplete. Reasoning alone, including reasoning hidden by summary: "none", cannot complete an agent turn. The gateway preserves reported token usage and emits response.failed rather than silently marking the response completed. It does not retry that request internally or change the selected model. The separate opt-in Messages empty completion recovery policy remains unchanged.

Repeated tool declarations

A long chat can declare the same tool more than once: in several Responses lite additional_tools input items, or in an additional_tools item and again in the current top-level tools list. The ChatGPT backend accepts this, so the gateway merges the declarations into its own catalog instead of refusing the request (duplicate_tool).

  • Identity. A function or custom tool is identified by its name, qualified by its namespace for a namespace tool (the default functions namespace is unqualified, like a top-level tool). Any other typed tool, such as tool_search, is identified by its type. The same local name in two different namespaces stays two tools.
  • Precedence. The current request's top-level tools win over any history declaration. Among additional_tools items a later item wins over an earlier one, and within one list a later entry wins over an earlier one. An exact duplicate is dropped; a differing one is replaced by the winner. A tool or its namespace keeps the position of its first declaration.
  • Scope. Only the gateway's own catalog is merged. On the Codex route the original input items still go upstream unchanged (apart from the tool_search drops below).
  • Telemetry. When anything merged, the gateway records tool_declarations_merged with the counts replaced and identical, once per request, never a name, definition or argument (diagnostics).

Malformed declarations still fail with their own reasons (invalid_shape, unsupported_tool) unless a valid declaration of the same tool supersedes them; only a repeated name no longer fails a request.

Tool search on the Codex subscription route

Native Codex rows can enable supports_search_tool, so the client sends a tool_search tool, declares it either at the top level or inside a Responses lite additional_tools input item, and later replays tool_search_call and tool_search_output items. The search itself runs in the client (execution: "client"): Codex searches its deferred tools and replays the matching definitions in tool_search_output. The ChatGPT backend refuses the tool_search type through the gateway's shared-subscription login (HTTP 400 subscription_sharing_unsupported_capability, quoted in hosted web search; first seen on 0.4.4, where every Codex 2 turn failed with "Provider returned HTTP 400"). Search is therefore off by default. A codex-subscription provider can opt in to a bridge with "toolSearch": "bridge" in gateway.json; "off" is the default, and any other provider type refuses the setting. gateway tool-search on, off and status set, remove and show it for every codex-subscription provider; the command validates the edited file before saving it and changes no other field. The setting is capability metadata, so a change applies live, without a rebind; a chat started before the change keeps its catalog until Codex loads the new one.

  • Codex subscription route, off. Before sending upstream, the gateway drops any tool_search tool, at the top level or inside an additional_tools item (an item left with no tool is dropped too), and any tool_search_call or tool_search_output input item. This covers an engine that still holds an older catalog with search on. The rest of the request is unchanged and keeps its order, including tool_choice, so the turn runs as it would without search. When anything was dropped, the gateway records tool_search_dropped with the count of tools and items (diagnostics).
  • Codex subscription route, bridged. The gateway sends search with tool types the backend accepts (src/protocol/tool-search-bridge.ts). The tool_search tool becomes an ordinary function with the same description and parameters, where it was declared: a top-level one joins the gateway namespace, and one inside an additional_tools item stays there. Its name is tool_search, or tool_search_ and so on when a flat tool already has that name. A replayed tool_search_call becomes a function_call of that function, and its tool_search_output becomes a function_call_output that names the loaded tools, followed by the loaded tools themselves: in a new additional_tools item right after the output on a Responses lite request, so everything before that point (and the prompt cache for it) is unchanged, and appended to the top-level tools otherwise. That item carries the role of the request's own additional_tools item (Codex sends developer), because the backend refuses one without a role. A tool already declared is not declared again, defer_loading is removed because the bridge loads the tool explicitly, and only function, custom and namespace tools are loaded. When the model calls the function, the client receives a tool_search_call with the parsed arguments and runs the search; it is never dispatched as a caller tool, an interrupted unfinished one is withheld like an unfinished function call, and invalid arguments fail as invalid_tool_call. Calls of loaded tools resolve like any caller tool. Codex resends the whole history every turn, so the gateway keeps no state. The gateway records tool_search_bridged with counts only.
  • Verification. node scripts/probe-tool-search-bridge.mjs --dry-run runs both rounds (the model searches, then calls the tool the search loaded) through the gateway's own provider code against a scripted backend, for a top-level and a Responses lite request, and checks that nothing of the tool_search type or defer_loading reaches the wire. Without --dry-run it makes the same four requests to the real backend. On 23 Oct 2026 all four completed: for both shapes the model called the search bridge, then called the fixture tool returned by that search. The dry run passed too. This establishes the bridge's real inference and replay behavior; it does not make the raw tool_search type supported by the subscription endpoint. The installed setting remains off until explicitly enabled.
  • Bridge risks. Loading tools on a request that is not Responses lite changes the top-level tool list, which can lower prompt cache hits from that point. The model sees a function rather than the tool type it was trained with, so it may use search a little differently. In the seven days before the bridge was built, no native Codex chat on the test Mac used tool search at all, so its benefit depends on connecting many deferred MCP or connector tools.
  • Upstream search items. If the upstream ever produces a tool_search_call or tool_search_output, it still streams back to the client as sent, once each; an interrupted final snapshot withholds a search item whose status is not completed.
  • Every other route. Claude, Copilot, Grok, chat-completions, anthropic-api and generic Responses routes drop the tool_search tool and both item types instead of rejecting them, so a chat that switches away from a Codex route keeps working. The tools an earlier search loaded stay declared (ranked below any tool the request declares itself), so the new model can still call them. Each drop is recorded as tool_search_dropped. A forced tool_choice: "required" with only the search tool has nothing to call there and still fails with unsupported_tool_choice. Anthropic Messages requests carry only function tools.
  • Catalog. supports_search_tool is published on only for a bridged route's rows, and a Codex 2 row keeps it on only when its native row has it on too. Every other row, and every native row carried for sub-agents, has it off, because a bare model name resolves to a route only when the request runs (details).
  • Ownership. The client executes search and owns the deferred tool list. The gateway never runs a search; it only changes how search items travel. Tool names, queries and outputs are never logged; failures record only the fixed reason and the allowlisted item type.

Hosted web search

Native Codex rows that carry web_search_tool_type send OpenAI's hosted web_search tool, and the ChatGPT backend accepts exactly that one hosted tool through a shared subscription: forwarding tool_search answers HTTP 400 subscription_sharing_unsupported_capability -- "User subscription sharing currently supports only 'web_search' and developer-defined 'function' and 'custom' tools, including 'namespace'" -- which is why tool search is not forwarded as such (it is off, or bridged as a function) while web search is forwarded.

scripts/probe-hosted-tools.mjs asks the backend directly, one short request per case, and records only status codes and fixed error fields. On 21 Oct 2026 it showed the refusal above for tool_search, and showed that web_search passed the backend's tool check. On 23 Oct 2026 a real request through ResponsesAPI completed with a completed web_search_call, establishing actual hosted search execution too. The earlier run showed that https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, which native Codex uses, answers 401 to the gateway's own login, so the gateway keeps https://api.openai.com/v1.

  • Codex subscription route. The web_search tool, declared at the top level or inside a Responses lite additional_tools item, is forwarded upstream unchanged and never wrapped into the gateway namespace, and replayed web_search_call input items go upstream as sent. A web_search_call the backend produces streams back to the client as received, once each, and an interrupted final snapshot withholds one whose status is not completed, as it does a search item. response.web_search_call.* progress events are ignored. A forced tool_choice: "required" counts a declared web_search as satisfying the call.
  • Every other route. Claude, Copilot, chat-completions, anthropic-api and generic Responses routes drop the tool and its replayed items before anything is translated or sent, so a chat that switches here from Codex 2 mid-turn keeps working; a tool_choice naming web_search drops to auto on those routes. When anything was dropped, the gateway records web_search_dropped with the count of tools and items (diagnostics) -- counts only, never a name, query or result. Every other hosted tool type (file_search, computer_use, image_generation, ...) keeps failing with unsupported_tool on every route, exactly as before.
  • Catalog. A Codex 2 row copies the native row's web_search_tool_type, so Codex sends the tool on it exactly as it does natively; Claude, Copilot and other rows lose the field, and supports_search_tool -- a different tool's flag -- stays off unless a route bridges tool search (details).
  • Ownership. The backend runs the search and the client renders its items. The gateway never runs a search itself and never logs a query or result.
